q: A school (Group 2 building) carries a PCC of P150,000,000. Applying the DAEDS bracket of P5,500,000 plus 4% of the excess over P100.0M, what Professional Fee results?
n: Group 2 DAEDS bracket for P100M—P200M: P5,500,000 + 4% of excess over P100M. Excess = P50M; 4% × P50M = P2,000,000. Total = P5,500,000 + P2,000,000 = P7,500,000.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 6.3, Group 2 DAEDS table
steps: Group 2 DAEDS bracket for P100M—P200M: P5,500,000 + 4% of excess over P100M.

q: A Group 3 hospital project carries a PCC of P300,000,000. Applying the DAEDS bracket of P11,500,000 plus 4% of the excess over P200.0M, what Professional Fee results?
n: Group 3 DAEDS bracket for P200M—P500M: P11,500,000 + 4% of excess over P200M. Excess = P100M; 4% × P100M = P4,000,000. Total = P11,500,000 + P4,000,000 = P15,500,000.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 6.3, Group 3 DAEDS table
steps: Group 3 DAEDS bracket for P200M—P500M: P11,500,000 + 4% of excess over P200M.

q: An industrial plant (Group 1) is contracted under DADS with a PCC of P120,000,000. Applying the DADS bracket of P2,700,000 plus 1.8% of the excess over P100.0M, what Professional Fee results?
n: Group 1 DADS bracket for P100M—P200M: P2,700,000 + 1.8% of excess over P100M. Excess = P20M; 1.8% × P20M = P360,000. Total = P2,700,000 + P360,000 = P3,060,000.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 6.3, Group 1 DADS table
steps: Group 1 DADS bracket for P100M—P200M: P2,700,000 + 1.8% of excess over P100M.

q: A single-detached residence (Group 4) has a PCC of P20,000,000 and is contracted under DADS at a flat 6% of PCC. What Professional Fee results?
n: Group 4 DADS is a flat 6% of PCC (architecture-only scope). 6% × P20,000,000 = P1,200,000.
steps: Group 4 DADS is a flat 6% of PCC (architecture-only scope).

q: A developer constructs 4 identical retail branches (Group 6, Repetitive Construction) from the same unamended plans. Given a full RPF of P5,000,000 for one such building, what fee applies to the 4th building?
n: Under Group 6, the 4th building and succeeding units are billed at 30% of the RPF for that building type. 30% × P5,000,000 = P1,500,000.
steps: Under Group 6, the 4th building and succeeding units are billed at 30% of the RPF for that building type.

q: An existing office building (Group 2) is undergoing renovation, with the renovation work priced at a PCC of P40,000,000, against a base DAEDS rate of 6% for Group 2 (PCC ≤ P50M). After the Group 9 renovation surcharge is applied, what total Professional Fee results?
n: The building is a Group 2 type (base DAEDS rate 6%), and renovation work under Group 9 is surcharged 150% of the applicable RPF: 6% × 1.5 = 9%. 9% × P40,000,000 = P3,600,000.
steps: The building is a Group 2 type (base DAEDS rate 6%), and renovation work under Group 9 is surcharged 150% of the applicable RPF: 6% × 1.5 = 9%.

q: An Architect is called as an expert witness for 3 scheduled court hearings, of which 2 are postponed and never take place. What is the minimum total fee owed across all 3 appearances?
o: P0 (no fee, since the hearings did not push through)
n: As an expert witness, the fee is not less than P5,000.00 per appearance, regardless of whether the scheduled hearing took place. 3 appearances × P5,000 = P15,000.
steps: As an expert witness, the fee is not less than P5,000.00 per appearance, regardless of whether the scheduled hearing took place.

q: A project's total Professional Fee (PF) comes to P10,000,000. What cumulative amount is owed to the Architect once the Schematic Design phase is complete?
n: Cumulative payment after Schematic Design completion is 20% of PF (5% signing + 15% schematic). 20% × P10,000,000 = P2,000,000.
steps: Cumulative payment after Schematic Design completion is 20% of PF (5% signing + 15% schematic).

q: A project's total PF is P8,000,000. Within 15 days of the contract being awarded to the winning Constructor, what cumulative amount should the Architect have received?
n: Within 15 days after award to the winning Constructor, cumulative payment reaches 90% of PF (based on the winning bid price). 90% × P8,000,000 = P7,200,000.
steps: Within 15 days after award to the winning Constructor, cumulative payment reaches 90% of PF (based on the winning bid price).

q: Under the Unit Cost Method, an office building has 5,000 sqm of GFA priced at a historical PCC of P25,000/sqm with a 5% PCC fee, plus 1,000 sqm of non-GFA area billed at 50% of the GFA rate. What is the TOTAL fee (GFA plus non-GFA)?
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 4.1.2, Unit Cost Method
steps: Non-GFA fee (50% of GFA rate): P625/sqm × 1,000 sqm = P625,000.

q: Under Group 7 (Housing Project, DAEDS), a housing project comprises 15 identical units. Given an RPF of P1,000,000 for the 1st unit alone, what is the TOTAL fee across all 15 units?
n: Units 2—10 (9 additional units) at 50% of RPF each: 9 × (0.5 × P1,000,000) = P4,500,000, plus the 1st unit's P1,000,000 = P5,500,000 for 10 units. For units 11—15 (5 additional units) at 40% of RPF each: 5 × (0.4 × P1,000,000) = P2,000,000. Total for 15 units = P5,500,000 + P2,000,000 = P7,500,000.
steps: Units 2—10 (9 additional units) at 50% of RPF each: 9 × (0.5 × P1,000,000) = P4,500,000, plus the 1st unit's P1,000,000 = P5,500,000 for 10 units.
For units 11—15 (5 additional units) at 40% of RPF each: 5 × (0.4 × P1,000,000) = P2,000,000.

q: A Group 2 building carries a PCC of P40,000,000 (within the ≤P50M bracket, base DAEDS rate 6%). The Architect qualifies as a Level 2 Specialist (+1.00%), the project employs BIM (+0.10%), and submittals are fast-tracked (+0.10%). What total Professional Fee results after these adjustments?
n: Sub-total rate = 6.00% base + 1.00% (Level 2 Specialist) + 0.10% (BIM) + 0.10% (fast-track) = 7.20%. Since PCC ≤ P50M, the fee is simply 7.20% × P40,000,000 = P2,880,000.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 6.3, Group 2; Annex D-style adjustment factors
steps: Since PCC ≤ P50M, the fee is simply 7.20% × P40,000,000 = P2,880,000.

q: A hotel (Group 3) is contracted under DADS with a PCC of P90,000,000. Applying the DADS bracket of P2,100,000 plus 3.6% of the excess over P50.0M, what Professional Fee results?
n: Group 3 DADS bracket for P50M—P100M: P2,100,000 + 3.6% of excess over P50M. Excess = P40M; 3.6% × P40M = P1,440,000. Total = P2,100,000 + P1,440,000 = P3,540,000.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 6.3, Group 3 DADS table
steps: Group 3 DADS bracket for P50M—P100M: P2,100,000 + 3.6% of excess over P50M.

q: A manufacturing plant (Group 1) is contracted under DADS with a PCC of P250,000,000. Applying the DADS bracket of P4,500,000 plus 1.2% of the excess over P200.0M, what Professional Fee results?
n: Group 1 DADS bracket for P200M—P500M: P4,500,000 + 1.2% of excess over P200M. Excess = P50M; 1.2% × P50M = P600,000. Total = P4,500,000 + P600,000 = P5,100,000.
ref: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210, Sec. 6.3, Group 1 DADS table
steps: Group 1 DADS bracket for P200M—P500M: P4,500,000 + 1.2% of excess over P200M.

q: A PCA works under a P50,000/month Retainer for 6 months. The Client separately requests one extra consultation falling outside the retainer's scope, billed at P1,000/hour for 8 hours. What is the PCA's TOTAL compensation across the period?
n: Retainer covers the minimum service obligation: 6 months × P50,000 = P300,000. The additional consultation (outside the retainer scope) is billed separately on an hourly basis: 8 hours × P1,000/hr = P8,000. Total compensation = P300,000 + P8,000 = P308,000.
steps: Retainer covers the minimum service obligation: 6 months × P50,000 = P300,000.
The additional consultation (outside the retainer scope) is billed separately on an hourly basis: 8 hours × P1,000/hr = P8,000.
